translations.literal: Ninth month: an edict ordered Minister of Education and Prince of Langye Daozi recorder of affairs for the six statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi joined the central recorder’s bench.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，苻堅弟融陷壽春。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Fu Jian’s younger brother Fu Rong took Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong seized Shouchun for the invasion.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，諸將及苻堅戰于肥水，大破之，俘斬數萬計，獲堅輿輦及雲母車。

translations.literal: Yihai day [Nov 18]: the various generals fought Fu Jian at the Fei River and smashed him; prisoners and heads numbered in the tens of thousands; Fu Jian’s palanquin and mica carriage were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Feishui broke Former Qin’s host and captured Fu Jian’s conveyances.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚申，詔衛將軍謝安勞旋師于金城。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, gengshen day [Dec 12]: an edict ordered General Who Guards the Army Xie An to feast the returning army at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An welcomed the victors at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，立陳留王世子靈誕爲陳留王。

translations.literal: Renzi day [Dec 4]: Sun Bao, heir apparent of Prince of Chenliu, was established Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenliu heir Sun Bao succeeded to his princely title.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚午，以寇難初平，大赦。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, gengwu day [Jan 22, 385 CE]: because the bandit peril had just been pacified, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Feishui amnesty marked restored calm.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍謝石爲尚書令。

translations.literal: General of the Central Army Xie Shi was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi took the secretariat’s head chair.

sentences.zh: 開酒禁。

translations.literal: The prohibition on brewing was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wine bans ended in celebration.

sentences.zh: 始增百姓稅米，口五石。

translations.literal: For the first time commoners’ grain tax was increased to five shi per person.
translations.idiomatic: The rice levy jumped to five shi per capita.

sentences.zh: 前句町王翟遼背苻堅，舉兵於河南，慕容垂自鄴與遼合，遂攻堅子暉於洛陽。

translations.literal: The former king of Juding, Di Liao, broke with Fu Jian and raised troops in Henan; Murong Chui came from Ye to join Liao, then attacked Fu Jian’s son Hui at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao’s Henan revolt drew Murong Chui; together they pressed Fu Hui at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊世奔還隴右，遣使稱籓。

translations.literal: Duke of Chouchi Yang Shi fled back to Longyou and sent envoys declaring submission.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi rushed west and renewed fealty to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月庚子，封武陵王孫寶爲臨川王。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, gengzi day [Feb 16, 385 CE]: Sun Bao, grandson of Prince of Wuling, was enfeoffed Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: A Wuling grandson, Sun Bao, received the Linchuan seat.

sentences.zh: 戊午，立新寧王晞子遵爲新寧王。

translations.literal: Wuwu day [Mar 6]: the son of Prince of Xinning Xi, Zun, was established Prince of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinning princely seat passed to Zun.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁建平等四陵。

translations.literal: Xinhai day [Mar 9]: visited four tombs including Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed again at the western tombs.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉牢之克譙城。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Liu Laizhi took Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi seized Qiao from Qin holdouts.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍桓沖部將郭寶伐新城、魏興、上庸三郡，降之。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Huan Chong’s officer Guo Bao attacked the three commanderies Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong and brought them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Bao folded the Han River triple cities.

sentences.zh: 二月辛巳，使持節、都督荊江梁寧益交廣七州諸軍事、車騎將軍、荊州刺史桓沖卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, xinsi, Huan Chong, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Jiang, Liang, Ning, Yi, Jiao, and Guang, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, xinsi, Huan Chong, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Jiang, Liang, Ning, Yi, Jiao, and Guang, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Jingzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂自洛陽與翟遼攻苻堅子丕於鄴。

translations.literal: Murong Chui from Luoyang with Zhai Liao attacked Fu Pi (Fu Jian’s son) at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui and Zhai Liao closed on Ye against Fu Pi.

sentences.zh: 三月，以衛將軍謝安爲太保。

translations.literal: Third month: General Who Guards the Army Xie An became Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An moved to grand mentor with honors.

sentences.zh: 苻堅北地長史慕容泓、平陽太守慕容沖並起兵背堅。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Northern Di Chief Clerk Murong Hong and Pingyang Prefect Murong Chong both raised troops and turned against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong brothers rose in Guanzhong against Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己卯，增置太學生百人。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jimao day [May 15]: one hundred more Imperial University students were added.
translations.idiomatic: The state academy grew by a hundred places.

sentences.zh: 封張天錫爲西平公。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen Liang ruler kept rank as Xiping duke.

sentences.zh: 使竟陵太守趙統伐襄陽，克之。

translations.literal: Ordered Jingling Prefect Zhao Tong to campaign against Xiangyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tong reclaimed Xiangyang for Jin.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將姚萇背堅，起兵於北地，自立爲王，國號秦。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s Yao Chang rebelled against Jian, raised troops in Northern Di, styled himself king, with dynastic title Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang broke away and founded Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑朔，崇德皇太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guichou day [Jul 12], new moon: Empress Dowager Chongde, Lady Chu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Regent empress dowager Chu died.

sentences.zh: 慕容泓爲其叔父沖所殺，沖自稱皇太弟。

translations.literal: Murong Hong was killed by his uncle Chong; Chong styled himself imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong murdered Hong and claimed Yan heir status.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊戌，遣兼司空、高密王純之修謁洛陽五陵。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, wuxu day [Aug 17]: concurrently Minister of Works, Prince of Gaomi Chunzhi was sent to repair sacrifice at the five Luoyang tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhi swept the lost northern imperial graves.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬康獻皇后于崇平陵。

translations.literal: Jiyou day [Aug 28]: Empress Kangxian was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu joined Chongping beside her consort.

sentences.zh: 百濟遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: Baekje sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje offered southern seas gifts.

sentences.zh: 苻堅及慕容沖戰于鄭西，堅師敗績。

translations.literal: Fu Jian and Murong Chong fought west of Ye; Jian’s army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong shattered Fu Jian west of the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 八月戊寅，司空郗愔薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuyin day [Sep 26]: Minister of Works Xi Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin died in office.

sentences.zh: 九月辛卯，前鋒都督謝玄攻苻堅將兗州刺史張崇于鄄城，克之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, xinmao day [Oct 11]: Vanguard Commander-in-Chief Xie Xuan attacked Fu Jian’s Yanzhou Inspector Zhang Chong at Juancheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan drove Zhang Chong from Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 甲午，加太保謝安大都督揚、江、荊、司、豫、徐、兗、青、冀、幽、幷、梁、益、雍、涼十五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Jiawu day [Oct 14]: Grand Mentor Xie An was added commander-in-chief of military affairs for Yang, Jiang, Jing, Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, Liang, Yi, Yong, and Liang—fifteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An assumed sweeping theater command over fifteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai, the first day of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinhai, the first day of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，河間王曇之薨。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Prince Tanzhi of Hejian died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Prince Tanzhi of Hejian died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以玄象乖度，大赦。

translations.literal: On yichou, because the dark celestial signs had departed from their proper measures, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, because the dark celestial signs had departed from their proper measures, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立前新蔡王晃弟崇爲新蔡王。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Chong, younger brother of the former Prince Huang of Xincai, was established as Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Chong, younger brother of the former Prince Huang of Xincai, was established as Prince of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 苻堅青州刺史苻朗帥衆來降。

translations.literal: Fu Lang, Fu Jian's Inspector of Qingzhou, led his followers and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang, Fu Jian's Inspector of Qingzhou, led his followers and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二月，苻堅將呂光稱制于河右，自號酒泉公。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Fu Jian’s Lü Guang assumed regency west of the River and styled himself Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang carved out the northwest as his own.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖僭卽皇帝位于阿房。

translations.literal: Murong Chong usurped the imperial title at Epang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong crowned himself at Epang Palace.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月甲午，謁諸陵。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, jiawu day [Feb 25, 386 CE]: visited the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Spring sacrifices swept the mausoleum row.

sentences.zh: 二月，立國學。

translations.literal: Second month: established the National University.
translations.idiomatic: A state academy opened at the capital.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守任權斬苻堅益州刺史李平，益州平。

translations.literal: Ren Quan, Administrator of Shu Commandery, beheaded Li Ping, Fu Jian's Inspector of Yizhou, and Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Quan, Administrator of Shu Commandery, beheaded Li Ping, Fu Jian's Inspector of Yizhou, and Yizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 三月，滎陽人鄭燮以郡來降。

translations.literal: Third month: the Xingyang man Zheng Xie brought his commandery to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyang flipped to Jin.

sentences.zh: 苻堅國亂，使使奉表請迎。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s state was in turmoil; he sent envoys presenting a memorial requesting escort.
translations.idiomatic: The beaten Fu Jian begged Jin for rescue.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉牢之及慕容垂戰于黎陽，王師敗績。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Liu Laizhi fought Murong Chui at Liyang; the royal army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi lost to Murong Chui on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙辰，劉牢之與沛郡太守周次及垂戰于五橋澤，王師又敗績。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, bingchen day [May 21]: Liu Laizhi with Pei Prefect Zhou Ci fought Chui at Five Bridges Marsh; the royal army was again routed.
translations.idiomatic: Second defeat followed at Five Bridges Marsh.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，太保謝安帥衆救苻堅。

translations.literal: Renxu day [May 27]: Grand Mentor Xie An led troops to rescue Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An marched ostensibly to aid the stranded Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 五月，大水。

translations.literal: Fifth month: great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Late spring floods returned.

sentences.zh: 苻堅留太子宏守長安，奔于五將山。

translations.literal: Fu Jian left Crown Prince Hong to guard Chang’an and fled to Five Generals Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian abandoned Chang’an for the hills.

sentences.zh: 六月，宏來降，慕容沖入長安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hong came to surrender, and Murong Chong entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Hong came to surrender, and Murong Chong entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，苻丕自枋頭西走，龍驤將軍檀玄追之，爲丕所敗。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Fu Pi fled west from Fangtou; General of Dragon Soaring Tan Xuan pursued him and was defeated by Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi outran Tan Xuan’s pursuit from Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 旱，饑。

translations.literal: Drought; famine.
translations.idiomatic: Parched fields brought hunger again.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，老人星見。

translations.literal: Dingsi day [Aug 24]: the Old Man star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man star rose—auspice of age.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，使持節、侍中、中書監、大都督十五州諸軍事、衛將軍、太保謝安薨。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Xie An, bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, grand commander of military affairs in fifteen provinces, guard general, and grand protector, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Xie An, bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, director of the Secretariat, grand commander of military affairs in fifteen provinces, guard general, and grand protector, died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以琅邪王道子爲都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Prince Daozi of Langye was made commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Prince Daozi of Langye was made commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 是月，姚萇殺苻堅而僭卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: That month, Yao Chang killed Fu Jian and illegitimately ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Yao Chang killed Fu Jian and illegitimately ascended the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 九月，呂光據姑臧，自稱涼州刺史。

translations.literal: September: Lü Guang seized Guzang and styled himself Liangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang seized Wuwei and claimed Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻丕僭卽皇帝位于晉陽。

translations.literal: Fu Pi usurped the imperial title at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi declared emperor from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁亥，論淮肥之功，追封謝安廬陵郡公，封謝石南康公，謝玄康樂公，謝琰望蔡公，桓伊永脩公，自餘封拜各有差。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, dinghai day [Nov 22]: rewards for the Huai-Fei merit—posthumously enfeoff Xie An Duke of Luling commandery, Xie Shi Duke of Nankang, Xie Xuan Duke of Kangle, Xie Yan Duke of Wangcai, Huan Yi Duke of Yongxiu; remaining enfeoffments differed by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Feishui heroes received ducal stacks—Xie kin and Huan Yi foremost.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏國仁自稱大單于、秦河二州牧。

translations.literal: That year Qifu Guoren styled himself Grand Chanyu and shepherd of Qin and He provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin’s Qifu Guoren proclaimed dual shepherdships.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月辛未，慕容垂僭卽皇帝位于中山。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, xinwei day [Feb 15, 387 CE]: Murong Chui usurped the imperial title at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan rose with Murong Chui’s throne at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，翟遼襲黎陽，執太守滕恬之。

translations.literal: Renwu day [Feb 26]: Zhai Liao raided Liyang and seized Prefect Teng Tianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao snatched Liyang and captured Teng Tianzhi.

sentences.zh: 乙酉。

translations.literal: Yiyou day [Feb 29].
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle marks yiyou.

sentences.zh: 謁諸陵。

translations.literal: Visited the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the season at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖將許木末殺慕容沖于長安。

translations.literal: Murong Chong’s general Xu Mumou killed Murong Chong in Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: A Yan officer murdered Murong Chong inside the fallen western capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，大赦。

translations.literal: Third month: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Spring brought another blanket pardon.

sentences.zh: 太山太守張願以郡叛，降于翟遼。

translations.literal: Taishan Prefect Zhang Yuan rebelled with his commandery and surrendered to Zhai Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan flipped to Zhai Liao’s coalition.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，以百濟王世子餘暉爲使持節、都督、鎮東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Baekje crown prince Yu Hui was appointed Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief, General Who Guards the East, and king of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje’s heir received Jin investiture and full general’s regalia.

sentences.zh: 代王拓拔圭始改稱魏。

translations.literal: King of Dai Tuoba Gui first changed his state title to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuoba ruler began calling his realm Wei.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以尚書僕射陸納爲尚書左僕射，譙王恬爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Guisi day [May 4]: Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Na became Left Vice Director; Prince of Qiao Tian became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na and Prince Tian split the secretariat’s two chairs.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，地震。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jimao day [Jul 3]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tremors returned.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以前輔國將軍楊亮爲西戎校尉、雍州刺史，鎮衛山陵。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Yang Liang, former General Who Assists the State, was made Colonel of the Western Rong and Inspector of Yongzhou, and was stationed to guard the mountain mausolea.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Yang Liang, former General Who Assists the State, was made Colonel of the Western Rong and Inspector of Yongzhou, and was stationed to guard the mountain mausolea.

sentences.zh: 秋八月庚午，封孔靖之爲奉聖亭侯，奉宣尼祀。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, gengwu day [Sep 2]: Kong Jingzhi was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengsheng village to tend Master Xuan’s sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A Confucius caretaker received a hereditary fief for the sage’s cult.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，安平王邃之薨。

translations.literal: Dinghai day [Sep 19]: Prince of Anping Suizhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Anping passed away.

sentences.zh: 翟遼寇譙，龍驤將軍朱序擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao raided Qiao; General of Dragon Soaring Zhu Xu struck him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu drove Zhai Liao from Qiao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，慕容垂破苻丕于河東，丕走東垣，揚威將軍馮該擊斬之，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Murong Chui defeated Fu Pi east of the River; Pi fled to Dongyuan; General Who Displays Might Feng Gai attacked and beheaded him, sending the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui finished Fu Pi; his head reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 甲申，海西公奕薨。

translations.literal: Jiashen day [Dec 6]: Duke of Haixi Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor Yi died in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 十一月，苻丕將苻登僭卽皇帝位於隴東。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Fu Pi’s officer Fu Deng usurped the imperial title east of Long.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng declared himself emperor on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月乙巳，以豫州刺史朱序爲青、兗二州刺史，鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, yisi day [Feb 13, 388 CE]: Yu Inspector Zhu Xu became Qing-Yan dual inspector, stationed at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu shifted north to guard the Huaiyin crossing.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: Dingwei day [Feb 15]: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: New-year amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，暴風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: Renzi day [Feb 20]: violent wind tore off roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: Gales damaged the capital suburbs.

sentences.zh: 戊午，慕容垂寇河東，濟北太守溫詳奔彭城。

translations.literal: Wuwu day [Feb 26]: Murong Chui raided east of the River; Jibei Prefect Wen Xiang fled to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang abandoned Jibei before Chui’s advance.

sentences.zh: 翟遼遣子釗寇陳、潁，朱序擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao sent his son Zhao to raid Chen and Ying; Zhu Xu drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhao’s eastern thrust failed against Zhu Xu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊辰，尊夫人李氏爲皇太妃。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, wuchen day [May 7]: Lady Li was honored empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s mother Li became imperial mother.

sentences.zh: 己丑，雨雹。

translations.literal: Jichou day [May 28]: hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ice hail battered the fields.

sentences.zh: 高平人翟暢執太守徐含遠，以郡降于翟遼。

translations.literal: The Gaoping man Zhai Chang seized Prefect Xu Hanyuan and surrendered the commandery to Zhai Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping rose for Zhai Liao under Zhai Chang’s coup.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯，束帛聘處士戴逵、襲玄之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guimao day [Jul 19]: silk bundles were dispatched to hire recluses Dai Kui and Xi Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The court wooed Dai Kui and Xi Xuanzhi with formal silk gifts.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛巳，立皇子德宗爲皇太子，大赦，增文武位二等，大酺五日，賜百官布帛各有差。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, xinsi day [Sep 15]: Imperial Prince Dezong was established crown prince; great amnesty; civil and military ranks advanced two grades; grand communal drinking five days; the hundred officials granted cloth in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Dezong’s installation came with nationwide celebration.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，復新寧王遵爲武陵王，立梁王㻱子和爲梁王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, wuwu day [Oct 22]: Prince of Xinning Zun was restored Prince of Wuling; Prince of Liang Jin’s son He was established Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Princely seats shifted—Zun back to Wuling, He to Liang.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，松滋太守王遐之討翟遼于洛口，敗之。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Songzi Prefect Wang Xiazhi campaigned against Zhai Liao at Luokou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiazhi checked Zhai Liao at the Huai mouth.

sentences.zh: 十三年夏四月戊午，以青兗二州刺史朱序爲持節、都督雍梁沔中九郡諸軍事、雍州刺史，譙王恬之爲鎮北將軍、青兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, wuwu day [May 22, 389 CE]: Qing-Yan Inspector Zhu Xu became Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief for Yong, Liang, and Hannan nine commanderies, Yongzhou inspector; Prince of Qiao Tianzhi became General Who Guards the North and Qing-Yan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu took Yongzhou while Prince Tian held the northern Yang theater.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，旱。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-month drought parched the crops.

sentences.zh: 乞伏國仁死，弟乾歸嗣偽位，僭號河南王。

translations.literal: Qifu Guoren died; younger brother Qian Gui succeeded the false throne, styling himself King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin passed from brother to brother under the Henan title.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，翟遼將翟發寇洛陽，河南太守郭給距破之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Zhai Liao's general Zhai Fa raided Luoyang, and Guo Ji, Administrator of Henan, resisted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, Zhai Liao's general Zhai Fa raided Luoyang, and Guo Ji, Administrator of Henan, resisted and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月戊子，濤水入石頭，毀大桁，殺人。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on wuzi, surging water entered Shitou, destroyed the great bridge, and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on wuzi, surging water entered Shitou, destroyed the great bridge, and killed people.

sentences.zh: 乙未，大風，晝晦，延賢堂災。

translations.literal: On yiwei, a great wind blew, daylight went dark, and Yanxian Hall suffered a fire.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, a great wind blew, daylight went dark, and Yanxian Hall suffered a fire.

sentences.zh: 丙申，螽斯則百堂、客館、驃騎庫皆災。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Zhongsi Zeba Hall, the guest lodge, and the cavalry general's storehouse all suffered fires.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhongsi Zeba Hall, the guest lodge, and the cavalry general's storehouse all suffered fires.

sentences.zh: 己亥，加尚書令謝石衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jihai, Xie Shi, director of the Secretariat, was additionally made guard general and granted establishment of office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Xie Shi, director of the Secretariat, was additionally made guard general and granted establishment of office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 庚子，尚書令、衛將軍、開府儀同三司謝石薨。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Xie Shi, director of the Secretariat, guard general, and holder of establishment of office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Xie Shi, director of the Secretariat, guard general, and holder of establishment of office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, died.

sentences.zh: 十四年春正月癸亥，詔淮南所獲俘虜付諸作部者一皆散遣，男女自相配匹，賜百日廩，其沿線爲軍賞者悉贖出之，以襄陽、淮南饒沃地各立一縣以居之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, guihai, in the fourteenth year, an edict ordered that all captives taken in Huainan and assigned to the various work offices be released, that men and women pair themselves with one another, and that they be given one hundred days of provisions; those along the line who had been used as military rewards were all to be redeemed, and one county each was to be established in the rich lands of Xiangyang and Huainan to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, guihai, in the fourteenth year, an edict ordered that all captives taken in Huainan and assigned to the various work offices be released, that men and women pair themselves with one another, and that they be given one hundred days of provisions; those along the line who had been used as military rewards were all to be redeemed, and one county each was to be established in the rich lands of Xiangyang and Huainan to settle them.

sentences.zh: 彭城妖賊劉黎僭稱皇帝於皇丘，龍驤將軍劉宰之討平之。

translations.literal: The Pengcheng sorcerer-rebel Liu Li usurped the title emperor at Huangqiu; General of Dragon Soaring Liu Zaizhi attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zaizhi crushed Liu Li’s roadside kingship.

sentences.zh: 二月，扶南獻方物。

translations.literal: Second month: Funan presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Funan sent southern tribute.

sentences.zh: 呂光僭號三河王。

translations.literal: Lü Guang assumed the title King of Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang’s Lü Guang took a river-king style.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲辰，彭城王弘之薨。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, jiachen day [May 22]: Prince of Pengcheng Hongzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng died.

sentences.zh: 翟遼寇滎陽，執太守張卓。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao raided Xingyang and seized Prefect Zhang Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao captured Zhang Zhuo at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 六月壬寅，使持節、都督荊益寧三州諸軍事、荊州刺史桓石虔卒。

translations.literal: Sixth month, renyin day [Jul 30]: Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, commander-in-chief of Jing, Yi, and Ning military affairs, Jingzhou Inspector Huan Shiqian died.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian’s death opened Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅，宣陽門四柱災。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, jiayin day [Sep 11]: the four pillars of Xuanyang Gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: Fire consumed Xuanyang Gate’s colonnade.

sentences.zh: 八月，姚萇襲破苻登，獲其偽后毛氏。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Yao Chang surprised Fu Deng and captured his false empress Lady Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang seized Fu Deng’s consort in battle.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，汝南王羲薨。

translations.literal: Dinghai day [Sep 23]: Prince of Runan Xi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Runan died.

sentences.zh: 九月庚午，以尚書左僕射陸納爲尚書令。

translations.literal: Ninth month, gengwu day [Oct 16]: Left Vice Director Lu Na became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na rose to director.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月乙巳，雨，木冰。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, yisi day [Jan 18, 391 CE]: rain—trees iced.
translations.idiomatic: Freezing rain lacquered branches white.

sentences.zh: 十五年春正月乙亥，鎮北將軍、譙王恬之薨。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, yihai day [Feb 25]: General Who Guards the North, Prince of Qiao Tianzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tian’s northern command ended with his death.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉牢之及翟遼、張願戰于太山，王師敗績。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Liu Laizhi fought Zhai Liao and Zhang Yuan at Taishan; the royal army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi lost Taishan to Zhai Liao’s alliance.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍朱序破慕容永於太行。

translations.literal: General Who Defeats Barbarians Zhu Xu defeated Murong Yong on the Taihang ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu broke Murong Yong’s Shanxi thrust.

sentences.zh: 二月辛己，以中書令王恭爲都督青兗幽幷冀五州諸軍事、前將軍、青兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, xinsi day [Mar 22]: Palace Secretariat Director Wang Gong became commander-in-chief for Qing, Yan, You, Bing, and Ji military affairs, former general, Qing-Yan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong took five-province command on the northern rim.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉朔，地震。

translations.literal: Third month, jiyou day [Apr 20], new moon: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Spring earth shook on the new moon.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，大赦。

translations.literal: Wuchen day [May 9]: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: May amnesty cleared debts of war.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁巳，有星孛于北河。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingsi day [Aug 15]: a broom star appeared in Northern River.
translations.idiomatic: A comet trailed through Northern River asterism.

sentences.zh: 八月，永嘉人李耽舉兵反，太守劉懷之討平之。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Yongjia man Li Dan raised troops in rebellion; Prefect Liu Huaizhi attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dan’s coastal rising fell to Liu Huaizhi.

sentences.zh: 己丑，京師地震。

translations.literal: Jichou day [Sep 7]: the capital region shook.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang felt an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 有星孛于北斗，犯紫微。

translations.literal: A broom star appeared in the Northern Dipper, encroaching on Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Cometary fire brushed the polar stars.

sentences.zh: 沔中諸郡及兗州大水。

translations.literal: Hannan commanderies and Yanzhou suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The Han River basin and Yanzhou drowned.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍朱序攻翟遼于滑台，大敗之，張願來降。

translations.literal: General of Dragon Soaring Zhu Xu attacked Zhai Liao at Huatai and smashed him; Zhang Yuan came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu broke Zhai Liao at Huatai and flipped Zhang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 九月丁未，以吳郡太守王珣爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Ninth month, dingwei day [Oct 15]: Administrator of Wu Wang Xun became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun entered the secretariat from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月己未，地震。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, jiwei day [Jan 6, 392 CE]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end tremors struck again.

sentences.zh: 十六年春正月庚申，改築太廟。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, gengshen day [Feb 17]: the Grand Temple was rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestors gained new shrine halls.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，慕容永寇河南，太守楊佺期擊破之。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Murong Yong raided Henan; Prefect Yang Quanqi defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Quanqi held Henan against Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 己未，章武王範之薨。

translations.literal: Jiwei day [Jul 17]: Prince Zhangwu Fanzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhangwu died.

sentences.zh: 秋九月癸未，以尚書右僕射王珣爲尚書左僕射，以太子詹事謝琰爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, guiwei day [Oct 13]: Right Vice Director Wang Xun became Left Vice Director; Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Xie Yan became Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun and Xie Yan rotated the secretariat wings.

sentences.zh: 新廟成。

translations.literal: The new temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral shrine stood finished.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，姚萇敗苻登于安定。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Yao Chang defeated Fu Deng at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin crushed Fu Deng’s northern remnant.

sentences.zh: 十七年春正月己巳朔，大赦，除逋租宿債。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, jisi day [Feb 8, 393 CE], new moon: great amnesty; delinquent rent and old debts remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen opened with debt forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，齊國內史蔣喆殺樂安太守辟閭濬，據青州反，北平原太守辟閭渾討平之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Interior Steward of Qi Jiang Zhe killed Lean Prefect Bikan Jun and seized Qingzhou in rebellion; Northern Pingyuan Prefect Bikan Hun attacked and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou briefly rebelled before Bikan Hun restored order.

sentences.zh: 五月丁卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dingmao day [Jun 7], new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Summer eclipse darkened the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯，京師地震。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guimao day [Jul 13]: the capital shook.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang quaked in summer heat.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，濤水入石頭，毀大桁。

translations.literal: Jiayin day [Jul 24]: surge waters entered Stone City and destroyed the great bridge.
translations.idiomatic: A tidal bore smashed the Stone City bridge.

sentences.zh: 永嘉郡潮水湧起，近海四縣人多死者。

translations.literal: Yongjia commandery’s tide surged; in four coastal counties many died.
translations.idiomatic: A tidal bore drowned Yongjia’s shore dwellers.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，大風，折木。

translations.literal: Yimao day [Jul 25]: great wind snapped trees.
translations.idiomatic: Windstorms followed the surge.

sentences.zh: 戊午，梁王龢薨。

translations.literal: Wuwu day [Jul 28]: Prince of Liang He died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang died.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂襲翟釗于黎陽，敗之，釗奔于慕容永。

translations.literal: Murong Chui surprised Zhai Zhao at Liyang, defeated him; Zhao fled to Murong Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Chui drove Zhai Zhao into Yong’s orbit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁丑，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingchou day [Aug 22]: Venus appeared in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Daylight Venus augured military stir.

sentences.zh: 八月，新作東宮。

translations.literal: Eighth month: a new eastern palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: Crown-prince quarters rose anew.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁酉，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, dingyou day [Nov 18]: Venus appeared in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Venus flared again by day in winter.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，都督荊益寧三州諸軍事、荊州刺史王忱卒。

translations.literal: Xinhai day [Dec 2]: commander-in-chief of Jing, Yi, and Ning military affairs, Jingzhou Inspector Wang Xin died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin’s death vacated Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸酉，以黃門郎殷仲堪爲都督荊益梁三州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, guiyou, Yellow Gates gentleman Yin Zhongkan was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Yi, and Liang, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, guiyou, Yellow Gates gentleman Yin Zhongkan was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Yi, and Liang, and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，徙封琅邪王道子爲會稽王，封皇子德文爲琅邪王。

translations.literal: Gengyin day [Jan 10, 394 CE]: Prince of Langye Daozi was transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Kuaiji; imperial son Dewen was enfeoffed Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi moved to Kuaiji while Prince Dewen took Langye.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，地震。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jiwei day [Jan 26]: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Another winter tremor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，自秋不雨，至于冬。

translations.literal: That year from autumn no rain fell until winter.
translations.idiomatic: Drought stretched from autumn into winter.

sentences.zh: 十八年春正月癸亥朔，地震。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, guihai day [Feb 15], new moon: earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: The new year opened with shaking earth.

sentences.zh: 二月乙未，地又震。

translations.literal: Second month, yiwei day [Mar 19]: the earth shook again.
translations.idiomatic: Aftershocks rolled through spring.

sentences.zh: 三月，翟釗寇河南。

translations.literal: Third month: Zhai Zhao raided Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhao probed Henan again.

sentences.zh: 夏六月己亥，始興、南康、廬陵大水，深五丈。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, jihai day [Jul 22]: Shixing, Nankang, and Luling flooded five fathoms deep.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Jiangxi drowned as before.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，旱。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: drought.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn dried what floods had spared.

sentences.zh: 閏月，妖賊司馬徽聚党于馬頭山，劉牢之遣部將討平之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: the sorcerer-rebel Sima Hui gathered a band on Matou Mountain; Liu Laizhi sent an officer to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hui’s hill band fell to Liu Laizhi’s detachment.

sentences.zh: 九月丙戌，龍驤將軍楊佺期擊氐帥楊佛嵩于潼谷，敗之。

translations.literal: Ninth month, bingxu day [Oct 28]: General of Dragon Soaring Yang Quanqi attacked Di chieftain Yang Fosong at Tong Valley and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Quanqi broke Di auxiliaries at Tonggu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，姚萇死，子興嗣偽位。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Yao Chang died; son Xing succeeded the false throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing inherited Later Qin from his father.

sentences.zh: 十九年夏六月壬子，追尊會稽王太妃鄭氏爲簡文宣太后。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, renzi day [Jul 14, 395 CE]: posthumously honored Lady Zheng, grand consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, as Empress Dowager Xuan of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu elevated his grandmother Lady Zheng to Xuan Dowager.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，荊、徐二州大水，傷秋稼，遣使振卹之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Jing and Xu provinces suffered great flood, damaging autumn crops; envoys were sent to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Floods ruined the lower Yangzi harvest; relief followed.

sentences.zh: 八月己巳，尊皇太妃李氏爲皇太后，宮曰崇訓。

translations.literal: Eighth month, jisi day [Sep 8]: Grand Imperial Consort Lady Li was honored empress dowager; her palace titled Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li moved from consort to mother-empress at Chongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂擊慕容永于長子，斬之。

translations.literal: Murong Chui attacked Murong Yong at Changzi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui ended Yan Yong at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，慕容垂遣其子惡奴寇廩丘，東平太守韋簡及垂將尹國戰于平陸，簡死之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Murong Chui sent his son Wu Nu to raid Linqiu; Administrator of Dongping Wei Jian fought Chui’s Yin Guo at Pinglu—Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian fell battling Murong raiders on the Shandong plain.

sentences.zh: 是歲，苻登爲姚興所殺，登太子崇奔于湟中，僭稱皇帝。

translations.literal: That year Fu Deng was killed by Yao Xing; Deng’s crown prince Chong fled to Huangzhong and usurped the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chong fled northwest and claimed the Qin flame.

sentences.zh: 二十年春二月，作宣太后廟。

translations.literal: Spring, second month of year 20 [396 CE]: built the shrine of Empress Dowager Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: A temple rose for Empress Dowager Xuan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，散騎常侍、光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、尚書令陸納卒。

translations.literal: Jiayin day [Mar 18]: Palace Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance, Household Grandee, office equal to Three Offices, Director of the Secretariat Lu Na died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Na’s long career ended.

sentences.zh: 三月庚辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third month, gengchen day [Apr 22], new moon: solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Spring eclipse on the gengchen new moon.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，荊、徐二州大水。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Jing and Xu provinces suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods swamped Jing and Xu again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏王拓拔珪擊慕容垂子寶于黍谷，敗之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Wei King Tuoba Gui attacked Murong Chui’s son Bao at Shugu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei bloodied Later Yan at Shugu.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春正月，造清暑殿。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of year 21 [397 CE]: built the Clear Summer Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace builders raised the Clear Summer retreat.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容垂攻平城，拔之。

translations.literal: Third month: Murong Chui attacked Pingcheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan seized Pingcheng from Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，新作永安宮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Yong’an Palace was newly built.
translations.idiomatic: Builders raised Yong’an Palace beside the seat of power.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，雨雹。

translations.literal: Dinghai day [May 14]: hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ice pellets crashed down on dinghai.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂死，子寶嗣偽位。

translations.literal: Murong Chui died; his son Bao succeeded to the false throne.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao inherited Later Yan after his father’s death.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，以望蔡公謝琰爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiazi day [Jun 18]: Wangcai Duke Xie Yan became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan moved from Wangcai county duke to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 大水。

translations.literal: Great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Floods spread across the lowlands.

sentences.zh: 六月，呂光僭卽天王位。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Lü Guang usurped the title Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang crowned himself Tianwang of Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 秋九月庚申，帝崩于清暑殿，時年三十五。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, gengshen day [Nov 6]: the emperor died in Clear Summer Hall; he was thirty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his lakeside hall at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 葬隆平陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Longping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: His tomb joined Longping beside prior rulers.

sentences.zh: 帝幼稱聰悟。

translations.literal: In childhood he was praised as clever and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he passed for brilliant.

sentences.zh: 簡文之崩也，時年十歲，至晡不臨，左右進諫，答曰：「哀至則哭，何常之有？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen died, he was then ten years old; by late afternoon he had not gone to mourn, and when attendants advanced remonstrance, he answered, "When grief arrives, then one weeps. What constancy is there in it?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen died, he was then ten years old; by late afternoon he had not gone to mourn, and when attendants advanced remonstrance, he answered, "When grief arrives, then one weeps. What constancy is there in it?"

sentences.zh: 謝安嘗歎以爲精理不減先帝。

translations.literal: Xie An once sighed that his refined judgment did not fall short of the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An compared his poise favorably to Yuan’s.

sentences.zh: 旣威權己出，雅有人主之量。

translations.literal: Once authority proceeded from his own person, he truly showed the measure of a sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held real power, he seemed capable of rule.

sentences.zh: 旣而溺于酒色，殆爲長夜之飲。

translations.literal: Afterwards he drowned in wine and women, nearly holding perpetual all-night revels.
translations.idiomatic: He sank into drinking and consorts and endless banquets.

sentences.zh: 末年長星見，帝心甚惡之，於華林園舉酒祝之曰：「長星，勸汝一杯酒，自古何有萬歲天子邪！」

translations.literal: In his final years, when a long-tailed star appeared, the emperor deeply disliked it. In Hualin Garden he raised wine and toasted it, saying, "Long-tailed star, I urge you to drink a cup of wine. Since antiquity, how has there ever been a Son of Heaven of ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: In his final years, when a long-tailed star appeared, the emperor deeply disliked it. In Hualin Garden he raised wine and toasted it, saying, "Long-tailed star, I urge you to drink a cup of wine. Since antiquity, how has there ever been a Son of Heaven of ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 太白連年晝見，地震水旱爲變者相屬。

translations.literal: Venus appeared in daytime year after year; earthquakes, floods, and droughts followed one another as portents.
translations.idiomatic: Omens stacked—daylight Venus, tremors, deluge, drought.

sentences.zh: 醒日旣少，而傍無正人，竟不能改焉。

translations.literal: Sober days were already few, and with no upright men at his side, he could not reform after all.
translations.idiomatic: Rare clarity and no honest counselors left him unreformed.

sentences.zh: 時張貴人有寵，年幾三十，帝戲之曰：「汝以年當廢矣。」

translations.literal: At the time, Honored Lady Zhang was favored and was nearly thirty years old. The emperor joked with her, saying, "Because of your age, you should be discarded."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Honored Lady Zhang was favored and was nearly thirty years old. The emperor joked with her, saying, "Because of your age, you should be discarded."

sentences.zh: 貴人潛怒，向夕，帝醉，遂暴崩。

translations.literal: The honored consort secretly raged; toward evening the emperor was drunk, and then he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: She murdered him that drunken evening—so tradition holds.

sentences.zh: 時道子昏惑，元顯專權，竟不推其罪人。

translations.literal: At that time Daozi was muddled and Yuanxian monopolized power—they never prosecuted the culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Simas Daozi and Yuanxian buried the truth.

sentences.zh: 初，簡文帝見讖云：「晉祚盡昌明。」

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Jianwen had seen a prophecy saying: “The house of Jin will end with Changming.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen once read a book prophecy tying Jin’s fall to “Changming.”

sentences.zh: 及帝之在孕也，李太后夢神人謂之曰：「汝生男，以『昌明』爲字。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was still in the womb, Empress Dowager Li dreamed that a spirit man said to her, "If you give birth to a boy, make 'Changming' his courtesy name."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was still in the womb, Empress Dowager Li dreamed that a spirit man said to her, "If you give birth to a boy, make 'Changming' his courtesy name."

sentences.zh: 及產，東方始明，因以爲名焉。

translations.literal: When he was delivered, the east had just brightened; therefore they used it as his formal name.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn at his birth became his personal name Yao tied to Changming.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝後悟，乃流涕。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen later understood and then wept.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen grasped the omen and wept.

sentences.zh: 及爲清暑殿，有識者以爲「清暑」反爲「楚」聲，哀楚之徵也。

translations.literal: When they built Clear Summer Hall, those who understood language thought “Clear Summer” reversed sounds like “Chu”—an omen of Chu’s lament.
translations.idiomatic: Wits said “Qingshu” punned on grief—clear summer echoing Chu sorrow.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝崩，晉祚自此傾矣。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died; from this Jin’s fortunes tilted.
translations.idiomatic: His death marked Jin’s downward turn.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前史稱「不有廢也，吾何以興」；

translations.literal: The historian says: earlier histories say, "If there had not been abandonment, how would I have arisen?"
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: earlier histories say, "If there had not been abandonment, how would I have arisen?"

sentences.zh: 若乃天挺惟神，光膺嗣位，邁油雲而驤首，濟沈川而能躍。

translations.literal: but when Heaven confers divine excellence and brilliant legitimacy receives the succession—vaulting oil-black clouds with head high, crossing sunken rivers yet able to leap—
translations.idiomatic: True restoration takes Heaven-touched heroes who ford chaos.

sentences.zh: 少康一旅之衆，所以闡帝圖；

translations.literal: Shaokang’s single brigade is what opened the royal plan;
translations.idiomatic: Shaokang’s handful of men rebuilt Xia.

sentences.zh: 成湯七十之基，所以興王業；

translations.literal: Cheng Tang’s seventy li foundation is what raised the kingly enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Tang rose from seventy square li.

sentences.zh: 靜河海於旣泄，補穹圓於已紊；

translations.literal: still river and sea after they had burst their banks, patching the round canopy after it was tangled;
translations.idiomatic: They dammed disaster and mended heaven’s frame.

sentences.zh: 事異於斯，則弗由也。

translations.literal: if events differ from this, then the way does not open.
translations.idiomatic: Without such heroes the path stays shut.

sentences.zh: 簡皇以虛白之姿，在屯如之會，政由桓氏，祭則寡人。

translations.literal: Emperor Jian, with empty-whiteness of bearing, in the crisis when hardship clung like mud—government issued from the Huan clan; at sacrifice he was the mere “orphaned man.”
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen reigned in name while Huan Wen ruled fact.

sentences.zh: 太宗晏駕，寧康纂業，天誘其衷，姦臣自隕。

translations.literal: When Taizong’s carriage halted, Ningkang inherited the enterprise—Heaven guided their inmost thoughts; traitorous ministers fell of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu’s death young Kuaiji-Zi’s reign saw Huan Wen’s threat expire by fate.

sentences.zh: 于時西逾劍岫而跨靈山，北振長河而臨清洛；

translations.literal: Then west of Sword Ridge they spanned Spirit Mountain; north along the long river they faced clear Luo;
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s arms reached Shu and the northern river.

sentences.zh: 荊吳戰旅，嘯叱成雲；

translations.literal: Jing and Wu hosts shouted until they became clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Yangzi armies massed like storm clouds.

sentences.zh: 名賢間出，舊德斯在：謝安可以鎮雅俗，彪之足以正紀綱，桓沖之夙夜王家，謝玄之善䉼軍事。

translations.literal: famous worthies appeared in turn, old virtue lingered: Xie An could steady refined custom; Wang Biaozhi could rectify statutes; Huan Chong served the royal house night and day; Xie Xuan was skilled at ordering military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An, Wang Biaozhi, Huan Chong, and Xie Xuan anchored state and camp.

sentences.zh: 于時上天乃眷，強氐自泯。

translations.literal: Then High Heaven looked down kindly and the mighty Di destroyed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored Jin while Former Qin collapsed.

sentences.zh: 五尺童子，振袂臨江，思所以掛旆天山，封泥函谷；

translations.literal: boys barely five feet brushed sleeves on the river, thinking how to plant banners on Tian Shan and seal Hangu with mud;
translations.idiomatic: Even children dreamed of reconquering the north.

sentences.zh: 而條綱弗垂，威思罕樹，道子荒乎朝政，國寶彙以小人，拜授之榮，初非天旨，鬻刑之貨，自走權門，毒賦年滋，愁民歲廣。

translations.literal: yet policy’s cords hung nowhere, awe and kindness rarely took root—Daozi wasted court governance, Wang Guobao piled petty men; honors of appointment were seldom Heaven’s decree at first; goods that bought punishments raced to powerful gates; poisonous levies grew yearly, the people’s sorrow widened each year.
translations.idiomatic: But Sima Daozi and Wang Guobao sold offices, poisoned taxes, and rotted administration.

sentences.zh: 是以聞人、許榮馳書詣闕，烈宗知其抗直，而惡聞逆耳，肆一醉於崇朝，飛千觴於長夜。

translations.literal: Therefore Wen Ren and Xu Rong rushed petitions to the palace; Emperor Suzong knew their blunt honesty yet hated to hear contrary words—he poured one morning’s drunkenness and hurled a thousand cups through the long night.
translations.idiomatic: Honest memorials went unheard while Xiaowu drank away warnings.

sentences.zh: 雖復「昌明」表夢，安聽神言？

translations.literal: Although "Changming" was shown in a dream, how could he have listened to the spirit's words?
translations.idiomatic: Although "Changming" was shown in a dream, how could he have listened to the spirit's words?

sentences.zh: 而金行穨弛，抑亦人事，語曰「大國之政未陵夷，小邦之亂已傾覆」也。

translations.literal: The decline and slackening of the metal phase was also perhaps a matter of human affairs. The saying goes, "Before the government of a great state has declined, the disorder of a small state has already overturned it."
translations.idiomatic: The decline and slackening of the metal phase was also perhaps a matter of human affairs. The saying goes, "Before the government of a great state has declined, the disorder of a small state has already overturned it."

sentences.zh: 屬苻堅百六之秋，棄肥水之衆，帝號爲「武」，不亦優哉！

translations.literal: He happened upon Fu Jian's season of one hundred and six and the abandonment of the masses at the Fei River, and the emperor's title was made "Wu"; is this not generous!
translations.idiomatic: He happened upon Fu Jian's season of one hundred and six and the abandonment of the masses at the Fei River, and the emperor's title was made "Wu"; is this not generous!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君若綴旒，道非交泰。

translations.literal: Encomium: The lord hangs like tassel-streamers; the Way was not one of intersecting peace.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler was pawn; harmony never fully came.

sentences.zh: 簡皇凝寂，不貽伊害。

translations.literal: Emperor Jian stayed still and silent—he did not hand down that calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen endured quietly without inviting catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 孝武登朝，姦雄自消。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu mounted the court, villain-heroes melted away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu’s early reign scattered warlords.

sentences.zh: 燕之擊路，鄭叔分鑣。

translations.literal: The Yan drum-road thundered; Zheng’s strains parted the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Triumph still echoed abroad while inner chambers slid toward Zheng-style indulgence.

sentences.zh: 倡臨帝席，酒勸天妖。

translations.literal: Singers mounted the imperial mat; wine toasted heaven’s prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Song girls shared his couch; cups fed ill omens.

sentences.zh: 金風不競，人事先彫。

translations.literal: Metal wind could not compete—human affairs withered first.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s fortune failed before Heaven’s judgment.
